name: Knowledge Domain
label: Divine Domain
summary: A scholar-priest who reads minds, borrows skills, and glimpses the history of any object.
flavor: The gods of knowledge value learning and understanding above all. Some teach that knowledge is to be gathered and shared in libraries and universities; others that it should be kept secret, doled out only to the worthy.
playstyle: The strongest out-of-combat utility domain, weak in a straight fight. Read Thoughts and Visions of the Past are investigation powerhouses.

features.name: Blessings of Knowledge
features.description: You learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in two skills of your choice from Arcana, History, Nature, and Religion — and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check using either of those skills.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
features.description: As an action, you choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes, you have proficiency with that skill or tool.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
features.description: As an action, choose one creature within 60 feet. It must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you can read its surface thoughts for 1 minute, gaining insight into its emotions and foremost concerns. As an action during that time, you can end the effect and cast *suggestion* on the creature without expending a slot — it automatically fails its save against that casting.

features.name: Potent Spellcasting
features.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

features.name: Visions of the Past
features.description: After at least 1 minute of meditation, you can call up visions of the past relating to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. *Object Reading* shows you the object's previous owners; *Area Reading* shows significant events that occurred within 50 feet in the past number of days equal to your Wisdom modifier. Each minute of concentration costs you one minute of the total; once you use the feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
